scope: Reject malformed DWG MESH face records that the existing typed geometry validator and DXF reader already refuse.

implementation.rule: DRW_Mesh::parseDwg requires each level-0 face record to contain at least three vertex indices before reading or publishing that face.
implementation.compatibilityBasis: DRW_Mesh::validateGeometry already requires face.size() >= 3 and the DXF MESH parser rejects face counts below 3. This keeps DWG input aligned with the model and other reader path; it does not claim that ODA v5.4.1 documents this DWG body.
implementation.failureBehavior: The existing fail path invalidates the frame, clears any prior or partial mesh state, and allows a later valid parse on the same object.

autodeskDxfReference.supports: MESH DXF group 93 gives the face-list size and group 90 carries face-list items; this reference does not state a minimum face cardinality.

autodeskSubDMeshApi.supports: The face array is a sequence in which each face starts with its vertex count followed by vertex indices; the API requires correct arrays but does not specify the minimum here.

research.odaSpecification: The ODA v5.4.1 PDF has no AcDbSubDMesh layout entry. No DWG byte-layout change or standards claim is based on that absent coverage.

coverage: Generated AC1024 triangle face stream reads with the expected ordered vertex indices.
Generated AC1024 two-index face is refused and clears stale/partial mesh state.
The valid triangle retries successfully on the same parser object after refusal.
Existing over-edge crease count refusal and corrected same-object retry still pass.
No DWG or DXF fixture files were added.

limitations: This closes a reader/model consistency gap and malformed-input case only.
Physical producer breadth, native MESH behavior, subdivision, topology, crease effects, and 3D semantic meaning remain unqualified.

repositoryState.stagedScope: bounded MESH DWG parse/output profile; DXF loss guards; generated vectors
